From f4f9fc29e56b6fa9d7fa65ec51d3c82aff99c99b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2021 20:55:36 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] nvme: fix the nsid value to print in
 nvme_validate_or_alloc_ns

ns can be NULL at this point, and my move of the check from
the original patch by Chaitanya broke this.

Fixes: 0ec84df4953b ("nvme-core: check ctrl css before setting up zns")
Signed-off-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

diff --git a/drivers/nvme/host/core.c b/drivers/nvme/host/core.c
index 82ad5eef9d0c..a5653892d773 100644
--- a/drivers/nvme/host/core.c
+++ b/drivers/nvme/host/core.c
@@ -4099,7 +4099,7 @@ static void nvme_validate_or_alloc_ns(struct nvme_ctrl *ctrl, unsigned nsid)
 		if (!nvme_multi_css(ctrl)) {
 			dev_warn(ctrl->device,
 				"command set not reported for nsid: %d\n",
-				ns->head->ns_id);
+				nsid);
 			break;
 		}
 		nvme_alloc_ns(ctrl, nsid, &ids);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/nvme/host/core.c`**
   - The line that printed the namespace ID (`ns->head->ns_id`) was modified to print the `nsid` value directly instead. This change was made in the `nvme_validate_or_alloc_ns` function.
   - The specific line changed was:
     ```c
     -				ns->head->ns_id);
     +				nsid);
     ```

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification addresses a bug where the `ns` pointer could be `NULL`, leading to a potential dereference error when trying to access `ns->head->ns_id`. By changing the print statement to use `nsid`, the code avoids this issue and ensures that a valid identifier is printed regardless of the state of the `ns` pointer.
- This change is a direct fix for a problem introduced in a previous patch (identified by the commit hash `0ec84df4953b`), which had moved the check for the command set without properly handling the case where `ns` could be `NULL`.
